items.title: 68514_Horace Henderson oral history interview
items.q: 'You'll have to relinquish your ownership of the band, and naturally your name, but I would like to use you in the band as pianist, and arranger

ctx.x: No, that isn't quite correct. I'll tell you. Don Redmond first was the director and arranger for the great McKinney's Cottonpickers Band in Detroit, Michigan, the Graystone Ballroom. And Don has been -- (inaudible) I should say, because it's past tense now -- was always aggressive in getting a good job. Don got a contract in New York City in a nightclub called Connie's Inn. He got the contract first, and began to search for the band, McKinney's so he gave his notice with the Cottonpickers as director. So

he found out that I was playing in a place in Columbus, Ohio called Valley Dale. I had an excellent band there, and he came over and came out and heard the band, and loved it. Then we talked about what he had in mind, and he said, "I have a contract in New York City at Connie's Inn, and he said, 'It's gonna be a long time contract. The Mills Brothers will be a feature there, and he said, 'You'll have to relinquish your ownership of the band, and naturally your name, but I would like to use you in the band as…
